items.title: George Benson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Then we finally moved – after a few weeks, we moved down to Manhattan, right down the street from the Apollo Theater, a club called the Palm Cafe, a big place. Every night, James Brown would come in, because he’d be working down the street. He would come in. Then, one night, he sat in with us. We knew all that stuff. That was like candy for me and Lonnie. Lonnie had been playing that for years. He couldn’t play no jazz, but he had great rhythm. James Brown was so impressed at what we could do, he said, “How’d you…
